concept.name: Event-driven backtest
concept.definition: A backtest in which a clock processes market, signal, order, fill, and portfolio events in timestamp order.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Each event updates state and may enqueue later events, preventing strategy logic from reading beyond the current time frontier.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: A 09:30 quote triggers an order event; a later trade event partially fills it and then updates cash.
